steps.title: Module boss
steps.body: Three functions over web-server log lines like `2024-05-01T10:00:03 GET /home 200 35ms`. Aim for code a Python reviewer would approve: comprehensions, built-ins, the right containers, no index loops.

steps.title: Parse
steps.prompt: Write `parse(lines)`, a **generator** that yields a dict per valid line: `{"time": str, "method": str, "path": str, "status": int, "ms": int}`. Skip blank lines and lines that do not have exactly 5 fields or whose status/ms are not numbers (ms ends in `ms`).
solution: time, method, path, status, ms = parts
yield {"time": time, "method": method, "path": path, "status": int(status), "ms": int(ms[:-2])}
template: LOG = ["2024-05-01T10:00:03 GET /home 200 35ms", "", "garbage", "2024-05-01T10:00:04 POST /login 401 12ms", "t GET /x abc 1ms", "t GET /y 200 fast"]
Dojo.check("parse is a generator", isinstance(parse([]), types.GeneratorType), "use yield")
hints: Unpack the five fields after checking the count.
`int(ms[:-2])` drops the `ms`; wrap conversions in `try`/`except ValueError`.

steps.title: Stats
prompt: - `"slowest"`: path of the slowest request (first one on ties), or `None`
- `"by_status"`: dict status to count, **sorted by status**
- `"avg_ms"`: average ms rounded to 1 place, or `0.0` when empty
- `"top_paths"`: the 2 most requested paths as a list (ties: first seen first)
`rows` may be any iterable (even the generator), so make one list first.
steps.starter: # parse from the previous step, then stats
solution: time, method, path, status, ms = parts
yield {"time": time, "method": method, "path": path, "status": int(status), "ms": int(ms[:-2])}
statuses = Counter(r["status"] for r in rows)
"errors": sum(1 for r in rows if r["status"] >= 400),
"slowest": max(rows, key=lambda r: r["ms"])["path"] if rows else None,
"avg_ms": round(sum(r["ms"] for r in rows) / len(rows), 1) if rows else 0.0,
"top_paths": [p for p, _ in Counter(r["path"] for r in rows).most_common(2)],
template: Dojo.eq("empty input", (0, 0, None, {}, 0.0, []), (e["requests"], e["errors"], e["slowest"], e["by_status"], e["avg_ms"], e["top_paths"]))
hints: `dict(sorted(counter.items()))` gives a dict in status order.
Guard `max` and the average with `if rows else ...`.

steps.title: Bursts
steps.prompt: Keep `parse` and `stats`. Write `error_bursts(rows, size)` returning a list of `(start_time, end_time)` for every run of **at least `size` consecutive** error rows (status `>= 400`), in order. Use `itertools.groupby` on "is this an error?".
steps.starter: # parse and stats from the previous step, then error_bursts
solution: time, method, path, status, ms = parts
yield {"time": time, "method": method, "path": path, "status": int(status), "ms": int(ms[:-2])}
statuses = Counter(r["status"] for r in rows)
"errors": sum(1 for r in rows if r["status"] >= 400),
"slowest": max(rows, key=lambda r: r["ms"])["path"] if rows else None,
"avg_ms": round(sum(r["ms"] for r in rows) / len(rows), 1) if rows else 0.0,
"top_paths": [p for p, _ in Counter(r["path"] for r in rows).most_common(2)],
for is_error, run in groupby(rows, key=lambda r: r["status"] >= 400):
template: Dojo.eq("single errors count with size 1", 3, len(error_bursts(parse(LOG), 1)))
hints: Turn each run into a list to get its length and its first and last times.
